intent: Two user asks, in order: (1) fix the navigation performance — coming from the home page, clicking into different modules sometimes shows long delays with just a black background; (2) make the hub a full-fledged, immersive game interface — a creative game-menu hub in the found-device fiction that unifies everything playable, because today it reads like a text-heavy brochure. Strategy findings: the black screen is App.tsx's single Suspense fallback (a dim 'Loading…' string over #070b14) shown while a lazy game chunk (14–217 KB raw) streams over the network; the hub unmounts during the fetch, nothing prefetches on hover, and the SW precache only masks repeat visits — hence 'sometimes'. The hub redesign follows the suite's own established fiction: M6.5/M6.6 made 'the signal desk' the shared language (dossiers, stamps, meters, shifts) — so the hub becomes THE OPERATOR'S CONSOLE, the desk itself. You arrive as the operator; every playable thing is a station of equipment on the desk: THE PHONE RACK (the anthology), THE FEED DESK (Scam Radar), THE LENS BENCH (Tell Exam), THE GLASSBOX LAB (both explorables, keeping their live computed paper previews — the strongest content on the page), THE ARCHIVE DRAWER (all six legacy pieces, collapsed into one place, which also kills the confusing NEW/LEGACY badge split), and THE OPERATOR BADGE (the season strip as your ID card, same localStorage reads, same od-id). Each station: hardware silhouette + status LED, product name (recognizability), ONE short line, record stamp (✓ signal/rank or UNPLAYED). Marketing CTAs and pillar essays die — the desk is the navigation; number keys 1–6 jump stations. The route fix is a branded boot: App-level fallback becomes the console boot screen (brand mark, scanline shimmer, 'BOOTING'; static under reduced-motion), a prefetchRoute() helper warms chunks on pointerenter/focus of every station link, and the hub idle-warms all route chunks once after mount (requestIdleCallback with timeout fallback).
